scope: Our versioned graph format: 27 block types, typed wiring, engineering units, revisions, validation and undo/redo.
Local browser GUI with block palette, wiring, properties, templates, zoom, minimap and diagnostics.
Deterministic scans, feedback memory, PI, timers, schedules, fault injection, timed scenarios and CSV traces. This is our graph runtime, not JCI firmware emulation.

2–16 graph instances with a common clock and typed/unit-checked previous-cycle links. All programs commit together; a failed cycle holds every state/output. Bounded sessions/history, quality fault records and portable workspace save/reopen. No field interfaces or equipment/firmware emulation.

Force any core graph block output, retain underlying block state, release individual/all overrides and record computed/forced values. Source faults still fail scans. Timed scenarios replay force maps; CSV includes override evidence. These holds are not exported as controller logic or sent to field devices.
Direct and transitive sources/consumers, affected outputs, previous-scan feedback boundaries, execution-order problems and click-through navigation for the portable core graph.

BMS JSON, IEC Structured Text, PLCopen TC6 XML with ST, GraphML and real native Sedona bundles/SAX/SAB/SCode. Studio files re-import with source consistency checks; a declared subset of foreign standard-kit SAX/SAB converts with an execution-difference report. External IEC compiler acceptance remains unverified.
Observed ZIP/XML containers: preserve all unknown data, jobInfo and simulationProperty entries; readable attribute/class dictionaries; original byte-exact export.
Narrow offline scalar patches to existing name/description/stored-value properties. Full block creation, rewiring, target compilation and native validation are pending.

New JCI CAF/CAP, ALC GFB/logic, Honeywell Spyder application and Niagara BOG/station encoders require verified semantics, compilers/packages and target tests. Sedona is implemented separately. No renamed JSON exports.

Pinned upstream compiler creates real kits, SAX, SAB and 64-bit simulator SCode. All 27 graph blocks run in a separate native VM, compared with the graph engine. Native online components/wiring persist through revisions and exports. Exported applications scan automatically; calendar/I/O mapping is a destination-runtime responsibility. Experimental local Unix port, not physical-platform certification.

Explicit unicast discovery, object/property reads, bounded object lists, command previews, priority-slot checks, verified writes, relinquish and durable command recovery. Tested with real loopback UDP.

Explicit router IP plus DNET/MAC addressing. NPDU routing passed an IP-to-virtual-data-link test. Physical MS/TP and E2/F2 remain untested. User supplied Tailscale access; connectivity checks are queued after programming completion.

BACnet/IP, Modbus TCP and Modbus RTU with enumerated serial ports. Real TCP sockets and OS pseudoterminal RTU tests cover fragmented replies and CRC rejection. Physical USB/RS-485 hardware remains untested.
Requires verified transport/protocol implementation and hardware tests; a generic serial connection is insufficient. Bluetooth firmware/download restrictions remain target constraints.

Graph replacement with state retention and rollback in our sandbox. Real Sox add/write/link/unlink/delete in an owned native SVM; shadow-VM preflight, configuration conflict checks, compensating rollback, persistent project save/export and value/link readback. Proprietary controller application changes remain pending.

Tailscale access supplied; no connectivity or field changes attempted. Checks must follow programming completion. A physical sensor test still needs a native application adapter, exact target/unused terminal, original backup and verified restoration.
Nine illustrative VAV graph examples include six FX/Metasys profiles. They are not certified Title 24 sequences or downloadable native CAFs.
Vendor manuals, source repository inventory, page-level evidence, feature requirements and explicit support gaps. Copyrighted reference PDFs and site files stay outside the code repository.
